source_review.notes: Reviewed current Microsoft OLTP, OLAP, and mixed-workload architecture guidance; DuckDB analytical design documentation; current TPC specification index; PostgreSQL 18 materialized-view and statistics documentation; and the primary HyPer paper. All eight final destinations returned HTTP 200. Product, benchmark, and research claims are explicitly scoped.

evidence: Checked lambda, achieved throughput X, concurrency N, latency T, examined/changed/returned bytes, freshness lag L, demand vector D, and interference ratio I notation.
Checked commit, capture, apply, refresh, cache, and query snapshot timestamps remain semantically distinct.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Capacity units are consistently labeled as a one-dimensional illustrative policy rather than fungible real resources.

evidence: Recomputed fixture classifications as checkout OLTP, margin OLAP, and dashboard mixed from declared boolean rules.
Recomputed examined rows as 3 and 25,000,000 for checkout and margin fixtures.
Recomputed analytical ceiling as 100 minus 70 equals 30 capacity units and freshness lag as 1,045 minus 1,000 equals 45 seconds.
Recomputed example interference ratios as 92/40=2.3 and 84/35=2.4.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Fixture thresholds and ratios are bounded examples, not sizing or classification standards.

evidence: Re-derived workload classification as a vector of purpose, access, concurrency, latency, freshness, consistency, and resource demand rather than table size or schema shape.
Re-derived end-to-end freshness as the sum of capture, transport, queue, apply, refresh, cache, and scheduling contributions under named timestamps.
Re-derived that a split analytical store exchanges execution isolation and specialization for copied-state, lag, replay, schema, and reconciliation obligations.
Re-derived interference ratio interpretation as observed degradation without causal attribution.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: No universal OLTP/OLAP threshold or architecture theorem is claimed.

evidence: Reviewed point analytical decisions, large transactional changes, skewed hot keys, empty/light load, bursts, peak overlap, cold/warm caches, and long snapshots.
Reviewed CPU, memory, cache, I/O, workers, locks, versions, temporary storage, maintenance, failover, and correlated-resource interference.
Reviewed capture/apply pause, replica lag, refresh failure, schema incompatibility, duplicate/reordered/deleted changes, backfill, restart, replay, and reconciliation.
Reviewed averages versus tails, rows returned versus examined, source commit versus consumer visibility, and consistent versus incompatible snapshots.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: The chapter requires explicit degraded behavior rather than assuming fresh or isolated reads.

evidence: Validated classification output against every declared finite fixture field.
Validated additive admission budget arithmetic and named transaction reserve.
Validated commit-to-visible timestamp ordering and exact 45-second lag.
The verifier matched exact nine-line stdout, empty stderr, and zero exit status.
invariant_checking.notes: The model does not simulate queues, database execution, resource coupling, replication, or failures.

evidence: Reviewed each classifier branch and confirmed all fixtures reach exactly one intended result.
Reviewed capacity subtraction under the explicitly stated one-dimensional additive assumption.
Reviewed freshness subtraction against named commit and visibility states.
Reviewed why isolated baselines plus overlap establish interference but require waits/resources for causal diagnosis.
proof_review.notes: No proof is claimed for a specific engine's correctness, performance, isolation, or freshness.

evidence: Separated workload descriptions from database products, row/column layouts, and normalized/star schemas.
Separated transaction semantics from physical operation size and analytical purpose from scan size.
Separated materialization from freshness, replicas from zero lag, and one logical dataset from one physical representation.
Separated internal benchmark experiments from compliant TPC results and performance evidence from production fitness.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: HTAP is presented as a design family whose guarantees and interference remain versioned, measured properties.

evidence: The standard-library finite workload model executed successfully through the repository verifier.
All eight final primary or official reference destinations returned HTTP 200 on 2026-08-30.
Front matter, section order, local links, ten examples, five exercises, five answers, and snippet expectations passed draft validation.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No live database, TPC benchmark, mixed workload, replica, materialized view, change pipeline, fault injection, or capacity experiment was executed.

conceptual_review.notes: The chapter consistently treats OLTP, OLAP, and mixed work as measured distributions with explicit correctness, latency, freshness, and resource semantics.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed workload inventory, service objectives, tail latency, admission, physical representation, shared-engine governance, summaries, replicas, separate stores, change correctness, failure recovery, benchmarking, and architecture exit conditions.

pedagogical_review.notes: The review sheet, finite classifier, ten contrasting cases, and five measurement/design exercises progress from terminology through interference diagnosis and reproducible architecture evaluation.

limitations: Internal authoring, official/primary-source, mathematical, bounded executable-model, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed. The chapter and model do not certify any live database; TPC result; OLTP, OLAP, or HTAP classification; capacity reservation; query plan; tail-latency objective; resource isolation; materialized view; replica freshness; change pipeline; reconciliation; fault recovery; cost; or production fitness.
